Title: Malaysian lorry driver arrested in Singapore over 800 cartons of smuggled cigarettes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 33-year-old Malaysian lorry driver was arrested after Singapore authorities discovered more than 800 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden beneath baskets of vegetables in his vehicle at the Woodlands Checkpoint.
The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), in a Facebook post, said the smuggling attempt was foiled on Oct 8.
"Officers detected irregularities in scanned images of the Malaysia-registered lorry.
"The vehicle, which was carrying a consignment declared as assorted vegetables, was directed for enhanced checks after an ICA image analyst spotted anomalies in the scans," it said.
It added that during the checks, more than 800 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes were uncovered hidden beneath baskets of vegetables in white trash bags, the authority said.
Photographs shared by ICA showed an Isuzu box lorry and several plastic baskets stacked inside its cargo compartment.
Other photographs showed cartons of cigarettes packed in white plastic bags, as well as a large quantity of cigarette cartons laid out following the seizure.
The Malaysian driver was arrested in connection with the attempted smuggling.
ICA said the suspect and seized items were handed over to Singapore Customs for further investigation.
The authority reiterated its commitment to safeguarding Singapore's borders while facilitating legitimate trade and travel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH aims to defend seats, eyes fresh gains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) aims to defend its existing seats while looking to capture several target seats through strategic efforts in the upcoming Melaka state election.
PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said their
baseline is to retain the seats they hold.
"At the same time, we are looking for golden opportunities to wrest several seats.
​"If our strategy hits the mark, it is not impossible to bring about change.
"We are realistic, but we see factors that could allow our targeted seats to shift to PH," he said after presenting Deepavali vouchers to 300 families in Taman Sri Sentosa today.
On Saturday, PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the coalition would
contest 21 seats
in the Melaka state election next month.
Of the total, PKR will contest nine seats, while DAP will field candidates in seven and Amanah in five.
​Fahmi said the coalition's Presidential Council met this afternoon to discuss election readiness following updates from Melaka PH leader Adam Adli ahead of nomination day on Oct 31.
​He added that the council was also briefed on the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly.
​"It is still too early, and we do not have specific dates yet. The Election Commission (EC) announced a meeting on Nov 6, so we have merely taken note of the dissolution," he said.
​Addressing media facilities for the Melaka campaign, Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said he will visit premises managed by the Information Department and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) in the coming days.
​He said MCMC is working with the EC to ensure stable internet coverage at all polling stations, supported by a network operations centre to monitor connectivity issues.
Fahmi added that a dedicated media centre will also be established, with further updates expected on Friday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asean envoy to visit Myanmar Wednesday - Thai FM
Article:
BANGKOK: Asean's special envoy for Myanmar, Philippines Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro, will visit Naypyidaw on Wednesday and Thursday, her Thai counterpart said.
There was no immediate indication of whether she would meet with former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi, who has been detained in Myanmar since being ousted in a 2021 military coup.
Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow – whose country is a member of the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) – told reporters in Bangkok on Tuesday that the itinerary "is being worked out."
Lazaro said in July she would visit Myanmar this year in an effort to expand access to humanitarian assistance in the country, which was plunged into civil war by the coup led by military chief turned civilian president Min Aung Hlaing.
Asean chair the Philippines had earlier this year requested "brief access" for its envoy to Suu Kyi, but was rebuffed.
In August, Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the first publicised meeting with a foreign official since her ouster.
In response, the Philippines called for the now 81-year-old's "complete and unconditional release", and repeated its request for access.
Sihasak said Lazaro's visit was timed to allow the envoy to report back to a meeting of Asean ministers ahead of a leaders summit.
"The details of her visit, the itinerary is being worked out," he said at a joint media appearance with his Malaysian counterpart.
"She is going there as the Asean special envoy, and we hope that there'll be good progress and some progress for her to report on when the Asean foreign ministers meet in Manila prior to the Asean Summit."
On Thursday, Suu Kyi's son Kim Aris was allowed to speak to her on the telephone for the first time in more than five years, in a call from Myanmar's London embassy.
The UK-based Aris told AFP afterwards that his mother had sounded "fairly healthy", but added: "I remain very concerned about her well-being."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Police probe Noorizwan custodial death as grievous hurt to obtain confession
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have reclassified the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly while in custody at the Cheras district police for voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort a confession.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the case was reclassified after a forensic expert confirmed that injuries found on Noorizwan's body were consistent with blunt force trauma and were not self-inflicted.
He said Bukit Aman's Prosecution and Legal Division (D5) had taken over investigations into the Oct 1 custodial death.
"The classification was made following a statement recorded from the forensic medicine consultant at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM), who conducted the post-mortem examination.
"The forensic expert confirmed the presence of external injuries on several parts of the deceased's body, with injury patterns consistent with blunt force trauma and not self-inflicted," he said in a statement tonight.
Section 331 of the Penal Code concerns voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort a confession or compel the restoration of property.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of 10 years and a possible fine upon conviction.
Kumar said the full post-mortem report to establish the cause of death had yet to be obtained as laboratory analysis was still pending.
He said police were awaiting further information from the hospital.
"Investigations are continuing to identify the police officers and personnel involved in handling and managing the deceased while he was detained at the Cheras district police headquarters.
"The investigation will be conducted thoroughly and professionally, without any element of a cover-up, to ensure that criminal justice is upheld in accordance with the law," he said.
Kumar stressed that police remained committed to transparency and integrity throughout the investigation.
He said the force would ensure impartial justice and would not compromise on any form of misconduct.
Noorizwan had been detained at the Cheras district police headquarters in connection with cases investigated under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Section 457 of the Penal Code and Section 379 of the Penal Code.
These provisions concern drug possession offences, housebreaking or trespassing to commit an offence, and theft, respectively.
On Sept 30, Noorizwan was referred to HCTM in Cheras for medical treatment.
He was pronounced dead at 1.52am on Oct 1.
Today, the family of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died in police custody at the Cheras district police headquarters, urged members of parliament to raise the matter in the
Dewan Rakyat
.
They also urged Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to clarify the status of the investigation into the case.
In addition, the family sought explanations regarding the injuries allegedly sustained by Noorizwan and the action taken against the policemen.
Noorizwan's younger sibling, Nooranis Zulkefly, said the family demanded justice for their brother's death, which had now entered its 27th day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration arrests 71 in passport forgery crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has arrested 71 people in 17 enforcement operations since 2024 in a crackdown on syndicates accused of falsifying passports to help foreign workers undergo mandatory medical examinations using other people's identities.
It released the figures after a Facebook post showing what appeared to be an altered Pakistani passport circulated again.
The post raised concerns about how foreign nationals could possess such documents and whether forged passports had been used to enter Malaysia.
The Facebook user claimed that foreign nationals had gone to a clinic with fake passports but left after a nurse questioned the documents' authenticity.
"How could they have entered the country using fake documents?" the user asked.
The post included images of what appeared to be altered passport photographs and had attracted about 2,500 reactions, 305 comments and 1,000 shares when viewed.
In a statement on its official Facebook page, the department said the same allegations had circulated widely in April this year.
It said intelligence gathering and enforcement operations since 2024 had uncovered syndicates involved in falsifying passports and altering personal information to help foreign workers undergo medical examinations using other people's identities.
"Since 2024, the department has carried out 17 enforcement operations and arrested 71 individuals in connection with document and travel document forgery activities," it said.
The department said the discovery of falsified passports in such cases did not necessarily mean the documents had been used to enter Malaysia.
The syndicates' modus operandi involved replacing passport photographs and altering personal details to help foreign workers undergo medical examinations using another person's identity, the department said.
The activities were linked to the renewal of Temporary Employment Visit Passes, particularly among foreign workers concerned about failing mandatory health screenings.
"By using another individual's identity, the workers could obtain medical examination results that met the requirements for renewing their employment passes," it said.

Title: Defence Ministry holds mental well-being programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: About 300 military and civilian personnel attended the Defence Ministry's Psychology Open Day to promote mental well-being, emotional resilience and a healthier workplace.
The event was complemented by the Madani Rahmah Sales Programme organised by Koperasi Media Prima, alongside entrepreneurial sales activities involving Felda and the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama).
The sales activities provided additional engagement opportunities for personnel attending the programme.
The event was organised by the ministry's Psychology Management Branch and officiated by Human Resource Management Division deputy secretary (services) Wan Norhazlina Wan Abdul Ghani.
It brought together armed forces personnel and civilian employees to raise awareness of mental and emotional well-being, strengthen interpersonal relationships and teamwork, and help employees cope with workplace stress and organisational changes.
Participants had access to psychological support services, health screenings and financial advice from eight participating agencies.
Among them was the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department's D11 Division, which conducted puppet therapy sessions.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia's Kuala Lumpur branch provided biofeedback therapy, while the National Population and Family Development Board offered rock therapy sessions.
The ministry's peer support group conducted psychological assessments, while healthcare personnel from the Titiwangsa District Health Office provided health screenings.
Other participating agencies included the Employees Provident Fund, the Zakat Collection Centre and Affin Bank, which offered financial services and consultations.
The programme also featured knowledge-sharing sessions on workplace motivation, mental well-being and financial fraud awareness.
Subang Jaya City Council cultural artiste Nurul Amira Mat Nasir delivered a session titled "Kerja, Jiwa & Cerita: Finding Joy in What We Do".
Affin Islamic Bank Berhad head of anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism compliance Yunos Yusop spoke on scam awareness.
Selangor Social Welfare Department psychology officer Md Aszulhilmy Ahmad Nahrawi shared advice on maintaining a positive mindset at work in a session titled "Mind Your Work: Fikir Baik, Rasa Baik, Kerja Baik".

Title: YNH unit settles LHDN tax dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: YNH Property Bhd's unit, YNH Construction Sdn Bhd has reached a settlement with the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN), paving the way for the withdrawal of a winding-up petition filed against it in March 2026.
The settlement resolves the dispute over outstanding tax liabilities following discussions between both parties.
YNH Property said at the High Court hearing on July 16 this year, no winding-up order was made against YNH Construction.
In a letter dated Oct 23, LHDN confirmed that the petition would be withdrawn following continued engagement between both parties.
Moving forward, the company said it remains focused on executing its ongoing property developments.
This includes Solasta Dutamas in Kuala Lumpur and its township projects in Seri Manjung, Perak, alongside broader capital management and asset monetisation initiatives.
YNH Property said it would provide further updates on any material developments through the appropriate disclosure channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HB Global unable to meet FY26 annual report deadline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HB Global Ltd will be unable to issue its annual report, comprising the annual audited financial statements and the auditors' and directors' reports for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), by Oct 30, 2026.
The deadline is prescribed under Paragraph 9.23(1) of Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd's Main Market Listing Requirements (MMLR).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the anticipated delay was mainly due to UHY Malaysia PLT withdrawing as its auditor for the financial period ended June 30, 2026, which affected the completion of the audit and finalisation of the annual report.
It added that the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority of Singapore (ACRA) had rejected its appeal on Oct 27, 2026, against the earlier rejection of its application to change its financial year-end from June 30, 2026, to Nov 30, 2026.
Following the decision, HB Global remains subject to the Oct 30, 2026 deadline to issue its annual report.
Under Paragraph 9.28(5) of the MMLR, if the company fails to issue its 2026 annual report within five market days after the reporting deadline expires, it will be subject to suspension.
Bursa Malaysia shall suspend trading in the company's securities on the next market day after the suspension deadline, in addition to any enforcement action it may take.
HLB Global said that, as Nov 9, 2026 (Monday) is a public holiday in conjunction with Deepavali, trading in the company's securities will be suspended from 9 am on Nov 10, 2026 (Tuesday), unless Bursa Malaysia determines otherwise.
The company said it will continue to assess and take the necessary measures to resolve the outstanding audit arrangements and complete its financial reporting obligations.
"The company will also continue to liaise with the relevant professional advisers and take the necessary steps in relation to the appointment of suitable auditors and the completion of the outstanding audit," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Leong Bank, Unionpay partner to facilitate cross-border payments in China
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Bank Bhd's (HLB) customers can now make QR payments at more than 120 million UnionPay and Weixin Pay merchant touchpoints across China through the HLB Connect application, following a strategic partnership with UnionPay International (UPI).
HLB group managing director and chief executive officer Kevin Lam said the collaboration would provide Malaysian travellers with greater convenience and confidence when making payments overseas, while laying the foundation for wider payment connectivity in other markets.
"At its core, a cross-border payment only works when trust exists on both sides of the transaction; where customers know with certainty that their payment will go through, and merchants know with certainty that they will receive the payment once it is made," he said at the launch of Ultimate Payment Passport with HLB event here today.
Lam said the partnership leveraged UPI's international network, including Weixin Pay, to provide customers with access to a wider merchant network directly through the banking application they already use in Malaysia.
He said HLB had conducted testing across various locations in China over the past month to ensure the payment experience worked effectively before the official launch.
The service is also available at participating merchants in Hong Kong, Macau and Thailand, with the bank looking to extend its payment connectivity to more destinations popular with Malaysian travellers.
Meanwhile, HLB managing director of personal financial services Andrew Jong said the service allows customers to make payments directly from their banking accounts without having to top up third-party e-wallets.
Jong said the service offered zero transaction fees, while customers could also draw from their Malaysian ringgit (MYR) wallet in the Pay&Save account.
"The combination of these different types of merchants, segments, and the duality of the consumer- and merchant-presented modes will allow you to access virtually 99.99 per cent of merchants across China," he said.
He said supporting both consumer-presented and merchant-presented QR payment modes was important because some merchants required customers to scan their QR codes, while others used scanners to read QR codes displayed by customers through their mobile applications.
Jong said HLB customers could also link eligible debit and credit cards to super-apps in China, including Weixin Pay, for payments involving services such as public transportation, food delivery, as well as food and beverage outlets.
He added that the partnership reflected the bank's efforts to expand its cross-border payment capabilities through digital innovation and collaboration with international payment networks.
In a statement, the bank said the feature complements its existing multi-currency facilities under the HLB Pay&Save Account, allowing customers to lock in favourable exchange rates ahead of their trips and avoid using third-party applications or topping up e-wallets.
HLB said its broader cross-border payment offering also includes direct debit and credit card payments, linking eligible cards to super-apps in China and using supported mobile wallets such as Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kulasegaran declines update on Teoh Beng Hock private prosecution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran has declined to give an update on the possibility of a private prosecution in the Teoh Beng Hock case.
He said the matter falls under the Attorney-General's Chambers and the police.
"Basically that comes under the A-GC. So I only answer in Parliament. I cannot say much," he told reporters after launching LAWYes, an artificial intelligence platform for legal practice, here today.
"It is the respective department who should do it," he said.
He said his portfolio covered amending laws, but the case was outside that scope.
"It's a police kind of thing. It comes under them. I don't want to speak for them," he said.
In July, Kulasegaran told the Dewan Rakyat he would seek clarification from the relevant agencies on further legal steps after the Attorney-General's Chambers classified the case as requiring no further action.
He said then that obtaining a fiat
could be considered
, adding: "There may be some legal process to compel the relevant agency to prosecute."
Beng Hock, the political secretary to then Seri Kembangan assemblyman Ean Yong Hian Wah, was found dead on July 16, 2009, at Plaza Masalam in Shah Alam after giving a statement at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission office.
His family filed a fresh legal bid in April to
compel the police
to investigate his death as murder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM270k in Budi Madani subsidies withheld over suspected abuse
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: More than RM270,000 in subsidy payments to a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, Penang, have been withheld after it was suspected of abusing the Budi Madani programme.
The Finance Ministry said more than 1,000 transactions involving over 100,000 litres of petrol had been recorded at the station using a manual bypass method.
The ministry said it acted after Budi Madani recipients discovered that their MyKad details had been used without their knowledge to buy subsidised petrol.
All had lodged police reports.
Besides withholding the payments, which remain subject to further reconciliation, the ministry has barred the station from selling subsidised RON95 petrol and diesel.
It did not name the station.
The station owner, family members and seven others — nine people in total — have also been barred from using the Budi Madani subsidy facility pending further action.
"Any subsidy abuse is a betrayal of the goal of targeted subsidies, especially when the conflict in West Asia continues to disrupt global energy supply and put pressure on fuel prices," the ministry said in a statement.
It said several other individuals suspected of being linked to the case had been identified, and their transaction records were being examined.
"If they are found to be involved in subsidy abuse, appropriate action will also be taken against them," it said.
In March, the ministry blocked the MyKad of a Malaysian seen in a
viral video
filling subsidised petrol into containers and barred the vehicle owner from the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme.
The ministry stressed that the subsidy was a privilege for the people and could not be misused for personal profit.
"The Madani government will not hesitate to take firm action against any petrol station or user found violating Budi Madani guidelines," it said.
Budi Madani is the government's targeted fuel subsidy programme, while Budi95 specifically covers subsidised RON95 petrol.

Title: Agoda, Adyen explore new payment services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Agoda and financial technology platform Adyen are exploring cooperation in payment issuing and payouts in selected markets, as the online travel platform looks to expand its payment capabilities.
The move comes as the companies mark more than a decade of collaboration, which began in 2015 when Agoda was expanding its mobile-first strategy across Asia.
Adyen now provides payment acquiring services for Agoda across multiple regions, supporting a range of local payment methods and currencies.
The companies have also worked to improve payment authorisation rates, reduce transaction costs and streamline checkout processes as Agoda expanded into more markets.
Their efforts include integrating local payment options, simplifying authentication for legitimate bookings and optimising payment routing to improve transaction reliability.
Agoda chief financial officer Oliver Webster said the partnership had evolved alongside the company's international expansion, with both sides focusing on payment reliability and customer experience.
He said these efforts supported Agoda's goal of making travel easier and more affordable.
Adyen Malaysia country manager Soon Yean Lee said the collaboration focused on improving payment routing, authorisation and settlement, with such improvements potentially having a significant impact given Agoda's transaction volumes.

Title: BMS Holdings expands northern reach with JV
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BMS Holdings Bhd has formed a joint venture with Wee Tatt Traders Sdn Bhd and its shareholders to expand its presence in the northern region of Peninsular Malaysia.
The joint venture will be undertaken through Jubin BMS (Wee Tatt) Sdn Bhd, which is 60 per cent-owned by BMS Holdings and 40 per cent by Wee Tatt's shareholders.
The joint venture company will be involved in the retail, wholesale and project sales of tiles, stone surfaces, bathware and kitchenware.
The partners will contribute a total of RM5 million to the joint venture, comprising RM3 million in cash from BMS Holdings and RM2 million in inventory from Wee Tatt's shareholders.
Wee Tatt's agreed business assets, contracts and employees are also intended for transfer to the joint venture, subject to the necessary consents and approvals.
The joint venture will operate from Wee Tatt's existing retail showroom and storage facility in Penang, providing an established operational base and workforce.
Wee Tatt, which trades in ceramics and related products, has been operating in Penang for more than 36 years.
BMS Holdings managing director Ang Kwee Peng said the northern region represented an important growth market for the company.
He said the partnership would combine Wee Tatt's local market presence with BMS Holdings' more than three decades of industry experience and broad product portfolio.
BMS Holdings will have management control of the joint venture, including the right to appoint a majority of its board members and the chairman.
As a 60 per cent-owned subsidiary, Jubin BMS' financial results will be consolidated into BMS Holdings' financial statements.
The company will fund its investment through internally generated funds and/or bank borrowings.
The partnership extends BMS Holdings' footprint beyond its existing network in Johor, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak.

Title: MMEA sailor killed off Perlis was devoted to duty, wife says
Article:
ALOR STAR: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer killed in a boat collision off Perlis last night was deeply committed to his duties, his wife said.
Sajaratul Akmal Abdul Shukor, 41, said her husband, Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, was always ready to serve regardless of the time or weather, even reporting for duty on his days off.
"He loved his job and would report for duty even on his days off. Sometimes, he would wake up at 2 or 3am to join an operation. I was used to it," she told reporters at the Forensic Department of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) here.
She said she understood the demands of his job with the Intelligence Unit at the Kedah and Perlis Maritime Headquarters.
Recalling their final conversation, Sajaratul Akmal said her husband had asked her to pray for his safety before he left for an operation involving undocumented migrants.
"He asked me to pray for his safety before the operation, which he had told me about two to three days earlier.
"He often spoke that way, so I never imagined anything bad would happen," she said.
She said she was shocked and devastated by the news, particularly because of its impact on their youngest child.
Mohd Roshaimi's remains were expected to be buried at the Muslim cemetery of Masjid Tengku Sarafudin Badlishah in Kuala Nerang tonight.
The incident occurred at about 11pm last night when an MMEA boat carrying five personnel collided with a concrete structure off Kuala Sungai Padang, near Kuala Perlis, while pursuing a vessel suspected of carrying undocumented migrants.
Three other sailors were injured. -- BERNAMA

Title: Bintai Kinden wins RM20.3mil TNB contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bintai Kinden Corporation Bhd has secured a RM20.28 million contract from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to extend two transformers at a substation in Pahang.
The mechanical and electrical engineering services provider said the project involves extending two transformers at the PMU Avetani substation, with completion expected within 540 days from the commencement date.
The contract brings the company's outstanding order book to RM183.8 million, providing earnings visibility in the near term.
Bintai Kinden also has a tender pipeline worth RM1.77 billion, comprising projects currently under evaluation across the mechanical and electrical engineering and construction sectors.
Managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Tay Chor Han said the contract win was an encouraging development that reaffirmed the group's commitment to rebuilding business momentum.
"Our recovery has been a journey of steady progress, and we believe that every contract secured represents another opportunity to demonstrate our capabilities, strengthen our track record and build confidence in our ability to deliver," he said in a statement.
Tay said with a substantial pipeline of tenders under evaluation, the company is actively working to translate these opportunities into new contract wins, which will further strengthen its order book and earnings visibility.
"We remain focused on delivering our projects to the required standards of quality, safety and efficiency, while continuing to pursue suitable opportunities in the market.
"We believe that consistent execution, operational discipline and a long-term commitment to our core mechanical and electrical engineering business will be key to our continued recovery and growth," he said.

Title: UMPSA to publish book on SMA scholar Siti Hawa
Article:
KUANTAN: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) will publish a book documenting the life and struggles of Dr Siti Hawa Apandi, who died today.
Vice-Chancellor Professor Ts Dr Yatimah Alias said the book would chronicle the spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) patient's journey, from her diploma studies in 2007 to completing her PhD last year.
"The book is being prepared with contributions from Siti Hawa's supervisors and UMPSA's Centre for Inclusive Technology and Ecosystem," she said today.
Siti Hawa, 37, was the country's first SMA patient to complete a diploma, bachelor's degree, master's degree and PhD at the same university. She died at her home in Taman Seri Mahkota Aman.
Her remains were taken to the Seri Mahkota Aman Mosque for funeral prayers before she was buried at the Batu 8 Muslim cemetery.
In August, she was recognised by the
Malaysia Book of Records
for completing all four levels of higher education at UMPSA.
Yatimah said Siti Hawa's academic achievements had made her an icon of inclusivity at the university, inspiring the campus community, particularly people with disabilities and inclusivity advocates.
"UMPSA's Centre for Inclusive Technology and Ecosystem director Dr Munira Abdul Razak had been following Siti Hawa's progress and published inspirational articles about inclusive ecosystems," she said.
SMA is a genetic disorder that damages motor neurons in the spinal cord, progressively weakening the muscles they control.

Title: Lawyers must not rely blindly on AI, says Kulasegaran
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lawyers must never rely blindly on information generated by artificial intelligence, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran.
He cited cases in Singapore where lawyers were ordered to personally pay costs after fictitious legal cases appeared in their court submissions.
"Such incidents remind us that lawyers must never rely blindly on AI generated information," he said at the launch of LAWYes, an artificial intelligence platform for legal practice, here today.
He said discussions on artificial intelligence in the legal profession must always be linked to service quality, responsibility and public trust.
"Artificial intelligence should not replace the judgement of a lawyer. It should strengthen the lawyer's ability to serve clients with greater accuracy, efficiency and care," he said.
He outlined three key considerations for lawyers adopting the technology, starting with accuracy and verifiability.
He said lawyers must ensure the authorities they cite actually exist and are relevant to the case.
"Responsibility for the work produced and for safeguarding the client's interests remains with the lawyer handling the matter.
"Technology may change how lawyers work, but it does not change their duty to the law, to the courts and, above all, to their clients," he said.
On confidentiality, he said clients must have confidence that their information is handled securely.
"As lawyers increasingly adopt AI, they must understand how client information is processed, stored and protected," he said.
He stressed the need for young lawyers, pupils in chambers and law students to keep developing their skills in legal research, drafting and independent analysis.
"AI should complement these skills, not replace them," he said.
LAWYes was developed by Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia Faculty of Law lecturer Associate Professor Dr Shahrul Mizan Ismail, who is also executive chairman of YF Associates Sdn Bhd.
The platform offers legal research assistance, document drafting and case-based workspaces, and is designed to reduce AI hallucinations by keeping its responses grounded in the legal materials available to it.
Kulasegaran said he was proud that LAWYes was a Malaysian innovation built from scratch by someone from a legal rather than technological background.
"We should not be content with merely using technology developed elsewhere. Malaysia must also have the confidence and capability to develop its own solutions," he said.
He also hoped lawyers would use the time saved through artificial intelligence to improve their wellbeing.
"If AI can help lawyers complete their research, drafting and other routine tasks more efficiently, I hope they will use the time saved not simply to take on more work, but also to take better care of themselves," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix AI stages 13.3pct rebound
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd shares rebounded 13.33 per cent to close at 8.5 sen amid speculative buying today, following months of heavy selling.
However, the cash-strapped technology group remains highly volatile after recent emergency talks with sukukholders failed to secure a waiver for a covenant breach involving its RM2 billion sukuk.
Prior to today's movement, forced selling from margin calls and an aggressive credit rating downgrade to junk status by MARC Ratings had wiped out over 90 per cent of Zetrix AI's market value.
An observer said the 13.33 per cent bounce is heavily technical, driven by speculative traders targeting a severely beaten-down stock.
Investor sentiment continues to process a massive corporate announcement where the board offered 788.83 million immediate-vesting employee share options, the observer added.
These options were priced at 5.4 sen,
representing a steep 28 per cent discount to the stock's baseline value which has created high speculative trading volumes.
Despite the stock recovery, the company faces structural headwinds.
Zetrix AI was recently suspended from its primary Road Transport Department collection role over RM314 million in unremitted government revenues.
This forced the company to scrap its upcoming dividend payouts to preserve operational cash.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt explores ways to sustain airlines, maintain connectivity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is exploring ways to help airlines remain sustainable and ensure connectivity is maintained, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
"We are trying to ensure the aviation industry is sustainable, and the government's priority is to ensure connectivity continues.
"The Finance Ministry is looking into the matter," he said when winding up the debate on the Transport Ministry's 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Loke said the government's priority was to keep national airlines operating, as the collapse of any major airline would affect connectivity.
"If an airline shuts down, it is not only the crew who lose their jobs. The bigger problem is connectivity.
"That would have a serious impact on the national economy.
"This issue remains a priority for the government, and we are doing our best to ensure it does not happen," he said.
Recently, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had made no agreement or commitment to provide financial support to low-cost carrier
AirAsia
amid financial difficulties linked to the Middle East conflict.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said applications for government support from companies in any sector were assessed based on the interests of the country and the people, the government's fiscal sustainability and the protection of public funds, in accordance with applicable laws and procedures.
AirAsia plays a significant role in Malaysia's air connectivity, particularly for domestic travel. The airline carried nearly 60 per cent of domestic passengers in 2025, with a large share of air connectivity in Sabah and Sarawak depending on its flights.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bukit Dinding set to become permanent forest reserve by November
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The gazettement of Bukit Dinding as a Permanent Forest Reserve is now at its final stage, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui.
He said the application to revoke the reservation of the open space at the site had been approved by the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Working Committee, while the gazettement process is expected to be completed by the end of November.
He said the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Lands and Mines Office director would prepare a draft gazette for the revocation of the open space reservation for review by the Attorney-General's Chambers before submitting it to the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Working Committee meeting chairman for signing, after which it would be published by Percetakan Nasional Malaysia Berhad.
"Once the gazette revoking the open space reservation has been published, the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Lands and Mines Office will notify the Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia so that the gazettement of the area as a permanent forest reserve under the National Forestry Act 1984 can be carried out," he said.
He was replying to a question from Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) on the latest developments in the gazettement of Lot 80026, Bukit Dinding, covering 20.57 hectares, as a Permanent Forest Reserve during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the Federal Territories Forestry Department had estimated a cost of RM116,000 for boundary surveys, initial management and public awareness programmes related to the proposed gazettement of Bukit Dinding.
He said no specific allocation had been provided for the purpose under Budget 2027. Instead, an application had been submitted under the project trust account.
Of the total, RM46,000 was estimated for surveying the boundary along a stretch of about two kilometres, RM20,000 for initial site management and RM50,000 for public awareness programmes, including awareness campaigns, initiatives with NGOs and Communication, Education and Public Awareness programmes.
Syed Ibrahim said the implementation of the work was subject to the completion of the process to revoke the government land reserve by the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Lands and Mines Office.
Following the revocation and re-gazettement processes, boundary surveying and marking, forest inventory and initial management work are expected to take about 10 months, from August 2027 to June 2028.

Title: Super El Nino: Hotter, drier weather in Malaysia from late Jan-March
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia may experience hotter and drier weather towards the end of the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon, especially from late January to March next year.
This is as the Super El Nino phenomenon could lead to reduced rainfall across the country
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said these conditions could increase the risk of heatwaves and droughts, especially if rainfall decreases during that period.
He said the El Nino phenomenon is currently in a strong phase and is expected to intensify to a very strong level or Super El Nino towards the end of this year and into next year.
"With reduced rainfall, hot weather or heatwaves often emerge, along with drought due to water shortages caused by insufficient rainfall," he said as a guest on Bernama TV's "Fokus 15" programme.
However, he said the initial phase of the monsson, which begins today, is expected to bring three to five episodes of prolonged heavy rainfall, particularly between this November and January 2027.
He said that these conditions could heighten the risk of flooding, particularly in the East Coast states of Kelantan, Terengganu and Pahang, as well as eastern Johor.
"Residents in flood-prone areas should remain vigilant regarding the risk of heavy rain during the early part of the monsoon, while drier conditions towards the end of the monsoon will require preparations for possible hot weather and water shortages," he said.
Maqrun Fadzli said MetMalaysia monitors weather developments around the clock and will issue heavy rain warnings when necessary to enable relevant agencies and the public to take appropriate precautionary measures.
He advised the public to always refer to latest weather information and warnings from official sources, make early preparations for possible floods and comply with instructions from the authorities, including evacuation orders when necessary.
He also reminded the public to avoid open burning during the dry weather to reduce the risk of localised haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Infomina bags contract for National Registration Dept's app systems
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd has secured a RM32.11 million contract from the Home Ministry to provide maintenance and technical support services for the National Registration Department's (NRD) core application systems.
The technology solutions provider said it accepted the letter of acceptance from the ministry on Oct 27, with the 24-month contract running from Nov 1, 2026, to Oct 31, 2028.
The contract, worth RM32.11 million excluding service tax, covers system maintenance, technical support, data and file management, user training, technical courses and review workshops.
Infomina said the contract is expected to contribute positively to its earnings over the contract period.
The contract win follows the company's financial performance in the first quarter ended Aug 31, 2026, during which revenue rose 39.6 per cent year-on-year to RM76.2 million, while net profit increased 27.3 per cent to RM12.6 million.
Its newly reported artificial intelligence solutions and data business services segment contributed RM8.4 million, or about 11 per cent of total revenue, reflecting progress in diversifying its revenue streams and expanding its technology capabilities.
Infomina chief executive officer cum managing director Yee Chee Meng said the contract reflects the continued confidence in Infomina's capabilities to manage and
maintain critical technology environments that support essential public-sector operations.
He added that beyond providing system maintenance and technical support, the company's scope also encompasses
data and file management, user training, technical courses and review workshops.
"These services will allow us to leverage our technical expertise to support the reliability and operational effectiveness of JPN's core application systems throughout the contract period," he said in a statement.
Yee said the latest contract further reinforces Infomina's track record in supporting mission-critical technology systems within Malaysia's public sector.
"We will continue to pursue opportunities across both the public and private sectors, leveraging our expertise alongside our expanding capabilities in applications, cloud, data, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and managed services," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dataprep executive chairman Wan Ahmad Rudirman resigns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dataprep Holdings Bhd has announced the resignation of its executive chairman, Dr Wan Ahmad Rudirman Wan Razak.
According to a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the information and communications technology (ICT) and payment solutions provider announced that the resignation, effective immediately, is due to personal reasons.
Wan Ahmad Rudirman was redesignated from managing director to executive chairman of the company on Aug 4, 2026.
He has over two decades of experience in corporate advisory, strategic investments, and regulatory oversight across public and private sectors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar vows tough action against migrant smuggling syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has vowed firm action against syndicates involved in smuggling foreigners into the country, as well as those who protect or abet them.
This follows the death of Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency intelligence officer Leading Seaman (Technical) Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, who was killed while trying to stop the entry of undocumented migrants.
"The lives of security personnel and the nation's sovereignty must not be gambled with," Anwar said in a social media post today.
He said he was deeply affected by Roshaimi's death and disappointed by the actions of those who threatened the nation's security and sovereignty.
"We cannot let this sacrifice be in vain.
"All enforcement teams must act firmly and without compromise against attempts to encroach on the nation's borders," he said.
Anwar added that those who allowed the country's sovereignty to be violated must also be brought to justice.
He and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, conveyed their condolences to Roshaimi's family and prayed that they would be granted patience and strength in facing their loss.
Anwar also extended his thoughts to all members of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency, who had lost a comrade in defending the security of the nation's waters.
Roshaimi, 41, was killed and three colleagues were injured after the
ir patrol boat crashed
while chasing a boat suspected of carrying undocumented migrants in the waters of Sungai Padang, Perlis.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ni Hsin proposes bonus issue of up to 312.65mil warrants
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd has proposed a bonus issue of up to 312.65 million warrants on the basis of one warrant for every two existing ordinary shares held by entitled shareholders.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the company, which specialises in stainless steel cookware and related products, said the warrants will be issued at no cost to entitled shareholders and will have a tenure of five years from the date of issuance.
Proceeds raised from the exercise of the warrants will be utilised for Ni Hsin's working capital and capital expenditure.
"The group intends to allocate 95 per cent of the proceeds to working capital, comprising the purchase of inventories such as electric vehicle motorcycles, batteries, charging cabinets and stainless steel coils, as well as marketing, after-sales service and administrative expenses.
"The remaining five per cent will be allocated to capital expenditure for the expansion of assembly lines, production and storage facilities," it said.
The company said the proceeds are expected to be fully utilised within 24 months from the date of receipt of the funds.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, it said the application to Bursa Malaysia for the exercise is expected to be made within two months from the date of the announcement, and the exercise is expected to be completed by the first quarter of 2027.
M & A Securities Sdn Bhd has been appointed as the principal adviser.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HSBC profits surge by a third as cost-cutting exceeds target
Article:
LONDON: HSBC has revealed its quarterly profits have leapt by nearly a third as it nears the end of a US$2 billion cost-cutting programme, reported PA Media/dpa.
The banking giant said it had made bigger savings than it originally set out to do.
It reported a pre-tax profit of US$9.6 billion for the three months to September, which was 32 per cent higher than the same period last year.
This was driven by it getting more income from interest rates, lower expected credit losses and a smaller provision for legal costs than the same period last year.
HSBC also announced it would be handing up to US$1 billion to shareholders as part of a new share buyback scheme.
It comes as the bank revealed its operating expenses - meaning the day-to-day spending of a business, including salaries - were US$1.3 billion lower than the same time last year.
It follows a major cost-cutting drive kickstarted by chief executive Georges Elhedery in 2025, who set a target to reduce the cost base by around US$1.5 billion a year by the end of 2026.
HSBC said it had beaten this target with cost savings worth US$1.9 billion, which it expects to reach US$2 billion by the end of the year.
Chief financial officer Pam Kaur said the cost savings have come from "a range of places" including the "deduplication of roles" which particularly impacted more senior positions.
She also said the bank was encouraging its staff to build their AI skills and be "future ready."
"And that's so important for us because, in our judgment, what's most important for an AI strategy to work is to keep the human accountability, judgment and decision-making very much at the core of what we do," she said.
"So AI is there to help humans, not necessarily to replace humans.
"We know that AI will change how work is done across industries and of course it will impact some roles, it will transform other roles, while creating entirely new roles."
It comes as reports said the bank was preparing to cut jobs in its UK wealth management business as part of efforts to ramp up the use of AI to serve wealthy customers more efficiently, according to the Financial Times.
Kaur said she would not comment on the speculation about job losses but that the bank "absolutely focuses on the workforce we have, both in terms of skilling it and building on it."
Elhedery said: "Our performance shows that in a more complex world clients continue to turn to us to navigate uncertainty and seize new opportunities.
"It also reflects consistent execution of our strategic priorities with pace, precision and discipline.
"As we simplify HSBC, we are creating greater capacity to invest, grow and deliver strong returns for our shareholders."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TuJu not designed to compete with Waze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The TuJu navigation app was never intended to compete with Waze, Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) chairman Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad said.
He said TuJu was developed with private app developers to upgrade MHA's Traffic Management Centre.
"Currently, we are not an app meant to compete with or be similar to Waze," he told the New Straits Times.
Last Wednesday, the government
barred civil servants from using Waze
, citing concerns over government information security and the potential misuse of users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's role as a data controller and its incorporation and operations under the laws of the country concerned.
The measure was intended to protect sensitive government information and citizens' personal data from potential exploitation that could threaten national security and sovereignty.
Hasni said TuJu operated only on toll and federal highways and was still under development.
"To expect TuJu to cover navigation on all roads in the country, it does not have the capacity," he said.
Users have complained about system failures and a lack of user-friendly features.
Despite a surge in downloads to more than 800,000, TuJu has fallen short of motorists' expectations.
A review found that the application, jointly developed by MHA and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd, was plagued by technical problems.
Hasni said motorists travelling on toll highways could use TuJu to check rest and service areas, identify available amenities, view emergency contacts and track traffic bottlenecks or accidents along their route.
He also said TuJu was an open platform with no sensitive security issues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eco-Shop posts higher Q1 FY27 net profit of RM63.19mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd's net profit for the first quarter of financial year 2027 ended Aug 31, 2026 (Q1 FY27) rose by 7.6 per cent to RM63.19 million from RM58.75 million posted in Q1 FY26.
Revenue also jumped by 16 per cent to RM793.67 million from RM684.33 million in the previous corresponding quarter.
The better results were driven by continued expansion of the group's store network, with the addition of 15 net new stores during the quarter, Eco-Shop said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
The company declared a single-tier interim dividend of 0.61 sen per ordinary share, amounting to approximately RM35.1 million, to be paid on Nov 27, 2026.
Chief executive officer Jessica Ng said the group continued to expand its store network, while same-store sales growth returned to positive territory, during 1Q FY2027.
"Alongside the continued expansion of its store network, Eco-Shop remains focused on enhancing the performance of existing stores.
"The store refresh programme supports this, together with the increasing adoption of data analytics to better understand Eco-Shop's members and engage with them more effectively through a new customer relationship management programme to be launched in the current financial year," she said.
Ng said that after opening 100 new stores in the previous financial year, Eco-Shop is targeting another 100 new store openings in FY2027.
"As the group continues to grow amid a backdrop of evolving operating costs, the focus remains on pursuing growth efficiently while maintaining a disciplined approach to cost management.
"Direct sourcing capabilities, economies of scale and financial discipline remain the cornerstones of  Eco-Shop's strategy to pursue sustainable and profitable growth while preserving the value proposition," she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China still tops list of international students in Malaysia, but other markets are growing, says EMGS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — While China remains Malaysia’s largest source of international students, the Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) said applications from other countries are growing.
EMGS chairman Datuk Ahmad Shalimin Ahmad Shaffie said China accounted for approximately 41 per cent of applications in 2023, but the proportion has since declined as Malaysia attracts students from more markets.
“By 2025, East Asia as a whole, including China, accounted for less than 37 per cent. In the first four months of 2026, China’s share stood at approximately 27 per cent.
“Alongside continued growth in total applications, these figures indicate an increasingly important contribution from other markets,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad Shalimin said regional figures further reflected this growing diversity.
“In 2025, applications from South Asia and Central Asia each grew by 41 per cent, while South-east Asia recorded 28 per cent growth, Africa by 20 per cent and the Middle East and North Africa by 19 per cent.
“Over the past decade, EMGS has received applications from 189 countries,” he added.
He said this was why the question raised by Gareth Liu Zi Yuan in his article, “More international students, but from where?”, published in Malay Mail on October 22, deserved attention.
“We welcome the discussion on broadening Malaysia’s international student community and ensuring that those who come here receive a rewarding education and experience.
“Malaysia is ranked 14th globally as an international education destination, welcoming students from nearly 180 countries. That reach provides a strong foundation,” he said.
However, Ahmad Shalimin said Malaysia must now strengthen existing connections, develop opportunities in underrepresented markets and ensure international students have good reasons to recommend the country after graduation.
He said EMGS conducts marketing activities across seven regions, with more than 50 programmes worldwide each year.
“Education fairs, forums, international exhibitions, school visits and counsellor engagements connect Malaysian institutions with students, families and education partners across different markets.
“Recent efforts have included Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Kenya, Türkiye and Central Asia, alongside participation in the European Association for International Education exhibition in Glasgow,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said engagement with neighbouring ASEAN countries, particularly Indonesia, and nearby regions such as South Asia remained a priority.
“These efforts also include creating more accessible pathways for students through mobility programmes and scholarship opportunities.
“By strengthening established partnerships while developing opportunities in emerging markets, Malaysia can broaden its international student community and build lasting education connections,” he said.
He added that student mobility programmes were also strengthening Malaysia’s ties with Europe.
“The number of mobility students from France increased from 827 in 2025 to 939 in 2026, a rise of 13.5 per cent, reflecting continued interest in Malaysia for short-term international study experiences,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said Malaysia’s international education presence was also expanding through local universities operating overseas.
“UCSI University’s campus in Dhaka, established in 2023, became Bangladesh’s first approved foreign university branch campus.
“It brings Malaysian education closer to students in their home country while strengthening the international presence of our institutions,” he said.
He said these developments reflected the growing international recognition of Malaysia’s higher education sector.
“Universiti Malaya is ranked 56th in the QS World University Rankings 2027 and joint 194th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027.
“Sunway University’s position as 11th globally for International Outlook in the latter rankings further illustrates the international engagement of Malaysia’s public and private institutions,” he said.
“For prospective students, these achievements help make Malaysia’s educational strengths visible. For our institutions, they reinforce the importance of sustained academic quality and international cooperation,” he added.
On student pass applications, Ahmad Shalimin said EMGS facilitates digital submissions, document verification, academic screening and application tracking, while the Immigration Department of Malaysia remains the approving authority.
“EMGS’s published processing charter is 14 working days for complete applications. Alya, our AI-powered assistant, also answers queries around the clock, helping students navigate visa requirements and application procedures.
“Upon arrival, the International Student Arrival Centres (ISAC) at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 provide round-the-clock assistance before immigration clearance, including guidance on access to dedicated lanes.
“This dedicated support helps students navigate their first experience in Malaysia with greater confidence,” he said.
He also said EMGS offered internship opportunities to international students, having welcomed interns from Iran, Myanmar, Indonesia, Turkmenistan and several African countries.
“These placements provide opportunities to apply knowledge, develop professional skills and experience a Malaysian workplace.
“Support from higher education institutions is equally vital through career guidance, industry partnerships and internship opportunities that prepare students for their future careers,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said internationalisation also benefited Malaysian students studying alongside their international counterparts.
“Shared classrooms, research and community activities expose students to different perspectives and help them build international networks within their own campuses.
“As Malaysian universities become better known abroad, employers and academic partners become more familiar with their qualifications and expertise.
“The relationships developed through education can support future research, institutional cooperation and professional opportunities,” he said.
He added that international graduates also helped strengthen Malaysia’s global connections.
“Their experiences influence what families, colleagues and future students understand about Malaysia. They become informal ambassadors whose achievements and personal stories give our higher education sector a human face,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said studying in Malaysia should offer international students more than just an academic qualification.
“Learning alongside people from different backgrounds, participating in community life and navigating new experiences can nurture empathy, resilience and a stronger sense of responsibility.
“Our ambition is for students to leave with the knowledge to pursue their careers and the character to contribute meaningfully to society, carrying a lasting connection with Malaysia wherever life takes them,” he said.
